Android provides the speaker and microphone to Linux PulseAudio. The platform query `capture-info` uses `$RUNGIC_PLATFORM_SOCKET`. It reports desktop visibility, microphone permission and whether a communication call holds the audio.

The Linux consumer is `shared/media/media-bridge.py`. It opens Android's microphone only while a Linux stream records from `android_microphone`. The desktop must also be visible and permitted. No call can be active.

The capture socket is `/mnt/android-wayland/capture.sock`, private to the app and container. A connection carries one request line, one header line, then raw PCM until it closes. Errors use {"error": string} before the header.

The `microphone` operation requires the exact header {ok, rate 48000, channels 1, format s16le}. The consumer refuses other headers. Android sends mono PCM. The consumer writes it to the `android_microphone` pipe source.

The `phone-output` operation requires the exact header {ok, rate 48000, channels 2, format s16le}. The consumer refuses other headers. It sends stereo PCM from the `android_phone` pipe sink. Android plays this on the phone itself, including while casting.

For communication operations, the consumer is `shared/media/communication-audio.cpp`, the provider of the communication-audio contract. A communication session changes Android to communication mode. `communication-output` sends a header, then packets containing an 8-byte epoch, a 4-byte length and mono PCM. Android discards packets from an older epoch.

`communication-control` sends a header, then JSON lines. Request {op: position, id} returns `ok`, `epoch`, `playedFrames`, `writtenFrames`, `rate` and the request ID. Request {op: flush, epoch: newer, id} returns the same fields plus `newEpoch`. `communication-microphone` sends a header, then mono PCM. Its header includes `aec`, which reports whether Android's echo canceller runs.

The default speaker, sink `android`, uses PulseAudio's native protocol instead of this capture protocol. It connects to Android-side PulseAudio (`system/android-audio`, `/mnt/android-audio/native`) through `module-tunnel-sink-new`.

Opening the microphone shows Android's indicator. Playback produces audible sound. Thus, the provider check sends only `capture-info`. Acceptance scenarios `audio.playback` and `audio.record` play and record on the phone.

`tools/tests/test_contract_media.py` checks `media-bridge.py` against the substitute in `tools/contracts.py`. Provider checks use acceptance scenarios `contract.audio`, `audio.playback` and `audio.record`.
